terms.term: The rent that HUD or the Contract Administrator has approved for each type of unit included in an assistance contract. The rent may be paid by the tenant, HUD or both parties.

A change made to Social Security and Supplemental Security Income benefits to counteract rising prices in the economy (inflation). It is typically equal to the percentage of the increase in the Consumer Price Index. If it is to be adjusted, the COLA is announced each October. However, the COLA increase is not reflected in the EIV data until the end of the calendar year.
Deceit or trickery used to gain an advantage dishonestly. Fraud is intentional and cannot be committed accidentally.
The gross rent is the sum of the contracted rent plus the utility allowance, if applicable at the property. For Section 202 PRAC and Section 811 PRAC, the gross rent is called the operating rent.

Created in the 1986 Tax Reform Act, this program gives state and local LIHTC-allocating agencies the authority to issue tax credits for the acquisition, rehabilitation or new construction of rental housing targeted to low-income households.

A federally mandated database housed with the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) that contains information about new job hirings, quarterly wages and unemployment insurance information. Employers are required by law to report their new hires to the state-level Directory of New Hires and their employees’ quarterly wages to the state workforce agency, which also collects unemployment data. The state and federal agencies report the data to the National Directory of New Hires. The NDNH data is used by state child support agencies and other authorized agencies (such as HUD and HUD-assisted property owners) to prevent overpayments, assess benefits, detect fraud and recover funds.

term.title: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

terms.term: A non-regulatory agency of the U.S. Department of Commerce that promotes American innovation and offers guidelines for technology-related standards, such as cybersecurity measures for adequately protecting data.

The timeline of reference used for income data collection to determine if a discrepancy exists between projected household income and actual income. In terms of discrepancy analysis, the POI start date is 15 months prior to the effective date of the form HUD-50059 (as reported in TRACS). The end date is 12 months from the start date.

The contract between the Owner and HUD that establishes the rights and responsibilities of the parties regarding the project and the payments under the PRAC. PRAC is used for Section 202 and Section 811 projects.

State, county, municipal or other governmental agencies or public bodies that are authorized to assist with the development or operation of low-income housing per the United States Housing Act of 1937.
An independent agency of the U.S. federal government that manages Social Security, the social insurance program that encompasses retirement, disability and survivor benefits.

Additional income payments made monthly to qualifying individuals, such as adults and children who have low income and resources, are blind or disabled. SSI can be received concurrently with Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI).

A computer system used by HUD, property Owners/Agents and authorized users for data certification, recertification and subsidy billing for multi-family subsidized housing. The system automates manual processes and controls to reduce rental assistance errors.
The total amount the tenant is required to pay toward the gross rent under the HUD rent formula.
The Secure Connection and Secure Systems required to provide protected access to HUD’s computer system via the internet.
